hook_line: I spent three years building the perfect productivity system.
why: Opens with credibility-then-subversion arc — elaborate system → exhaustion → 'the system became the work' — delivers a complete reframe in under a minute with no missing setup.

hook_line: The habit that changed everything didn't happen in the morning.
why: Pattern interrupt against morning-routine content dominance, lands on a vivid personal scene (nodding at wife, not actually hearing her) that converts an abstract productivity idea into felt emotional cost.

hook_line: The third habit is old advice, but most people miss the constraint that makes it work.
why: Curiosity gap on a universally known tip ('eat the frog'), immediately pays off with the one-frog constraint and reframes avoidance as an interest payment you pay all day — punchy, self-contained.

hook_line: Here is something that's changed how I measure a day.
why: Reframes the core problem of to-do lists (permanent deficit state) and offers a concrete counter-practice (done list), ending on a lasting insight about perception and planning — no prior context needed.

hook_line: The night before write exactly three priorities for tomorrow. Not five.
why: The 'not five' line lands as a bold, counterintuitive constraint immediately, the segment ends with a satisfying before/after scene (opening email vs. sitting down and writing) that proves the habit works.
